cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I accept your apology for breaking my vase. Now tell me when you knew the dog hadn't done it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Straight away. I'll buy you another vase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your money. You watched me shut the dog out of this room for three days. That is the part you're going to put right.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was embarrassed to admit it. Shall I let him back in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Call him in and give him his bed back. Then tell me why your embarrassment was easier to live with than mine when I found out I'd punished him for you.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 receives apology and demands explanation; A3 directs repair beyond broken vase; A5 authorizes return and names A shame, but adds an unestablished withheld bed.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 immediate knowledge; A5 uses B4 offer to let dog in, yet give bed back adds a separate deprivation not stated.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers replacement and B4 offers actual access repair, making B a plausible participant.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands B4 embarrassment excuse into A later shame; the bed adds unsupported detail rather than earned heightening.

specificity.evidence: A1 vase and A3 room exclusion are clear; A5 withheld bed is not established by that exclusion.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 long comparison has emotional force but unnecessary bed detail clouds it.

coach2.firstDefect: A5 give him his bed back adds unsupported prior action.
